must_find.item: Customers on monthly contracts churn more often than those on annual contracts.
must_find.quote: The analysis does not establish whether month-to-month (or any specific) contract type carries higher churn risk.
must_find.reason: The report finds contract significantly associated with churn but explicitly says the direction (monthly vs annual) was not reported or established.

must_find.item: Higher monthly_fee is associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: Churned and retained customers differ in monthly fee at the 5% level. The direction of the difference (whether churners pay more or less) was not reported, and the magnitude is unknown.
must_find.reason: It reports a significant difference but gives no direction, so it does not state that higher fees go with more churn.

must_find.item: More support_calls are associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: The significance result is reported but its supporting output is not shown, so treat it as provisional until verified.
must_find.reason: The report relates support_calls to churn as significant but gives no direction and treats it as unverified.

must_find.item: region shows no meaningful association with churn.
must_find.quote: Region has no detectable association with churn.
must_find.reason: The report states region shows no association with churn (p = 0.448).

must_not_claim.item: region is a significant or important predictor of churn.
must_not_claim.quote: Region is not useful for targeting. Consistent with the null chi-square result.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says region is not associated with churn, rejecting the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Annual-contract customers churn more often than monthly-contract customers.
must_not_claim.quote: Targeting decisions should not be made on the assumption that a specific contract type is the high-risk group.
must_not_claim.reason: The report never claims annual-contract customers churn more; it declines to state direction.
